They are fairly stiff in the ankle - but in a good way - you don't want to roll your ankle. One of the biggest problems that I remember with having rental skates in the past is that my feet turned inward, in these skates my feet were straight and in the right position (i.e., skating directly on the blade, instead of the side). Can't say whether that was due to the skates or my technique, but these were FAR better than any rental skates I've used. They're pretty comfy, I may add an insole for extra comfort. All in all these are excellent skates.
I took them to a skate shop and had them sharpened before I skated with them (about thirty bucks, but it was a pro shop and it seemed like they did a good job and it was worth the money!). Not sure if that was necessary, but a friend who is a serious skater said that you should always get your skates sharpened if they're brand new. (The guy at the skate shop said so, too.)
Remember to buy skate guards and to completely dry off your blades!

text_fidelity_a:
Aoneky Adjustable Kids Jump Rope with Counter and Comfortable Handles This is a nice lightweight adjustable jump rope with foam grips and a counter. The foam covering the hollow plastic covers makes the handles very comfortable, and also help you maintain a grip when your hands get sweaty. This jump rope comes with a 9.18 ft long adjustable foam rope that can accommodate individuals as tall as 5.9 feet.

The rope can be shortened by pulling an end through the black plastic holder at the top end of the handles until it's at the right size, but that may leave a LOT of excess rope dangling down on each side if you're adjusting it for a child for example. That excess foam rope has no place to go except to flap around with each swing of the rope most likely striking the child with each jump, so when I adjusted it to work for my granddaughter I cut the rope (which is easy to cut). Once the rope is cut it's not really possible for the rope to be used by a taller person as well, so I prefer the way excess rope can be tucked into the handle on this Aoneky rope better: [[ASIN:B00V7VE2BE Aoneky Lightweight Jump Rope with Comfort Handle]].

I think that the handle of this rope is as comfortable as the other rope's handles are, but they seem more durable than the other ones and I believe this one will outlast the other ones. The counter feature is a huge plus for everyone interested in knowing how many jumps they can achieve, whether it be for fitness, dieting, or simply to know if you're the school jump rope champion. The counter is located in the top portion of a handle (see my photo). Be sure to press the black tab to zero it out before jumping so you get an accurate count.

The counter function is a bit quirky - here's what we observed during testing:

1. Right hand operation: Counts upwards from zero (1, 2, 3 etc...) when the rope is jumped from back over the head to the front, and counts backwards if you jump with the rope from the front to the back.

2. Left hand operation: Jumping with the rope from the back over the head to the front causes the counter to count down from 999 (998, 997 etc), jumping the opposite direction causes the counter to count upwards (998, 999 etc).

The manufacturer recommends the counter be operated from the right hand only. This is a nice lightweight jump rope that seems to be built to last a long time and the handle grips are very comfortable. The counter works as long as you understand it's quirks, and the only fault I can find is that the rope is adjustable but the only way to really adjust it much shorter is to cut it, so I wish they would reconfigure the handle to have one end open to tuck excess rope into it like their other model allows in which case this rope could truly be adjustable without having to be cut.

Retail sample was provided by the manufacturer for consumer product evaluation, testing, and review purposes.
text_fidelity_b: Aoneky Adjustable Kids Jump Rope with Counter and Comfortable Handles

Tour Edge Bazooka 360 Men's Varsity Box Full Set, Right Hand, Black/Blue At first, I was very excited I’m able to get a well-known golf brand for my son’s first complete set. I’ve had Tour Edge drivers and fairway woods before (Exotics line), love the quality. But in this set, it left a lot to be desired. The quality is reminiscent of knock off brands: on some clubs (mainly the woods and hybrid) paint on the heads were misaligned, surfaces looked wavy, some zippers on the bag wouldn’t close because the tracks were off, and some other minor things not worth mentioning. Aside from many quality issues, the one that stood out the most are the dents on some club faces. This is a brand new set, why does it have dents? The bubble wrap and packaging were acceptable and it looked well packaged, there’s no reason for having dents. Quality issue? I’ve had clubs that were at least 10 years old and have been beat up; aside from superficial scratches, those clubs still were dent-free and serviceable. The set is slightly more expensive than some no-name beginner sets but I’m thinking the quality could be comparable. I get it, it’s a teen set, but I expected better quality control from the Tour Edge name. As I’m writing this, I’m actually pondering if this could be a knock off set, I hope not.
The good thing is that it is a complete set, the irons were of better quality it seems, and although the bag seems flimsy, it’s very light and will help with walking the course.
text_fidelity_b: Tour Edge Bazooka 360 Men's Varsity Box Full Set, Right Hand, Black/Blue

High Sierra Karadon Frame Pack, Amethyst/BlackBerry/Orchid, 30L (S-M) As far as looks go, this backpack is really nice! If a backpack can be called "lovely", I'd have to say that about this one. It's well made and appears very sturdy. It looks to be a high quality backpack.

I think all body types will be different, but for me, this backpack is comfortable to wear. The shoulders and hips have extra padding, so it doesn't rub into those parts. There's plenty of adjustable straps to make it more likely to fit each person just the way they need it to. The padding on the hips and shoulders are also removable, so you can (hand)wash those parts most likely to get sweaty and stinky. I haven't washed these parts yet, but right now they are attached very well. You have to really pull it to get it off, but it's not so hard that you're going to pull a muscle.

There's a rain guard attached within one of the pockets, so you can easily keep the backpack and your belongings dry if it rains. (This is the bottom pocket and the zipper is on the underside of the backpack.) There's extra room in there if you wanted to store anything with the rain guard. The middle space within the backpack is accessed from both the top and the middle, and it is open the whole length of the backpack. It is very roomy, and can be expanded with the 4 adjustable straps on the sides. (2 on each side) There's also a pocket behind the main one. Though it's not as roomy as the middle space, it still gives you lots of extra space. There's a pocket(without zippers or extras) on each side also. Each side of the hip strap has a little zippered pocket and one without a zipper. There's also a zippered pocket on the top cover. There's lots of adjustable straps all around, and also a couple of hooks.

Overall, this is a super nice and comfortable backpack, and I think most ladies will be extremely pleased with it.

text_fidelity_a:
SUBOOS Compact 3-in-1 Rechargeable LED Camping Lantern and Flashlight - 290 Lumens, Waterproof, Great for Suvival Kit, Emergency, Hurricane, Power Outage. We sometimes have seasons of power outages where I live. That is not a problem sometimes, but if it is a long extended one, it is handy to have lights available to use so we can continue life as normal as much as possible, especially in unlit areas like bathroom and basement. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This light is quite compact, yet large enough to stand up on the table. It has a hanging wire on the top of it that folds down. There is a round cloudy covering on the bottom, and a clear reflective opening on the top for the flashlight. There are curved textured see through coverings which are for red lights either constant or flashing.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This is really quite handy. A quick press will turn on the basic light. Another press, medium. Another press, high. One more press. Off. The light is pretty easy to see with and makes a great light if you have to work hands free at a table, or near metal surface which it will magnetically stick to.

FLASHLIGHT
The flashlight has two rapid presses and then one more will turn it brighter then off.

RED LIGHT
If you need to use a red light or need to attract attention you can use the red light consistent or flashing.

BOOKLET
The booklet in the package is well written and has great instructions how to use this.

CHARGING
The charging cord is USB to mini USB cord. There are five blue lights on the side and they will light up as the light is charged. When done, they stay lit until you unplug it.

LONGEVITY
We got several hours out of this on medium and high and it still has half a charge. It charges up pretty quickly in only a couple of hours, and you can use this with a power bank if you need to.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This magnetized light can either stand up on a table, stick to a metal surface, or hang by the wire from a string, hook, etc. It is plenty bright enough to use for emergencies or camping and lasts quite a few hours prior to having to charge again.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a great light to have handy, but over time, if anything changes, I will update. For now, it is performing well and lasts a good amount of time prior to needing a recharge.
text_fidelity_b: SUBOOS Compact 3-in-1 Rechargeable LED Camping Lantern and Flashlight - 290 Lumens, Waterproof, Great for Suvival Kit, Emergency, Hurricane, Power Outage.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa 3 Health & Fitness Smartwatch with GPS, 24/7 Heart Rate, Alexa Built-in, 6+ Days Battery, Black/Black, One Size (S & L Bands Included) Now that I have used this Fitbit for a few weeks I feel like I have an idea about it. I've wanted a Fitbit for years, I've heard nothing but amazing things about it and how great they are. Well, to be honest, I am not seeing the greatness of them now that I actually have one. Maybe it's because this is the newest one, maybe there are still bugs to fix, and maybe it could be my phone that just hates everything about the Fitbit app. Honestly, I don't know but either way, I am so unimpressed with this Fitbit.

The pros I have found out is that it was easy to set up and make an account with Fitbit. Everything downloaded, updated, and whatever else perfectly. It was easy to change all the settings and personalize everything the way I wanted it. I love that you can customize the face so that it matches your personality or the types of apps or stuff you want it to show first right on the face. I like that you can control your music and pay for your watch too. Those are great ideas and honestly if I got out more and whatever else I can see where tons of people would totally get so much use out of it.

My biggest beef I have with this though is the fact that I wear it constantly and I want to keep up mainly with my steps, how much I move, and my sleeping patterns. It doesn't have any problems keeping up with all of that and so much more. The problem I have with this watch is the fact that it disconnects from the wifi and then becomes difficult to sync to the app, if at all. I've already had to reset to factory settings once to get it to reconnect to the app, which also has its own set of challenges because once the watch goes the app doesn't want to do much either. I can't remove the watch to re-add it in the app and I'm unable to view the wifi connections to change them or re-add them. It's like everything stops and becomes completely unusable. It's a real pain, to say the least.

Being completely honest, the watch I replaced with this Fitbit was way better and I never had any issues with it syncing to my phone, the app, or anything else. It did everything that this one does but just not as pretty, which honestly I'd much rather the watch to work and do what I want it to do than to have the cool face and whatever else.

I am so unimpressed and honestly bummed about this watch not living up to the hype. I am hoping that everything works out and the bugs are fixed soon if these are bugs, but I've no idea. Right now the watch is acting up again and honestly, I am thinking I am about to have to reset it again. If this happens I am going back to my old one that I know works just fine. Honestly, don't waste your money on this one just yet but wait to see if the bugs are fixed in a few months.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa 3 Health & Fitness Smartwatch with GPS, 24/7 Heart Rate, Alexa Built-in, 6+ Days Battery, Black/Black, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Minn Kota Endura C2 30 Freshwater Transom Mounted Trolling Motor (30" Shaft) What I meant by the catchy headline is that this is about the minimum horsepower for the small boat application. In my case I have it hooked to a Sun Dolphin 8.5 play boat. My calculation was that more power was not only not needed, but not wanted. I need those lower speeds for trolling and such. Also I need to make sure that when I go out I can get back in, less paddle.

Here is the deal. The thing is NOT a power hog. As of this writing (super rainy wet year) I have battled winds and currents in our overflowing rivers and having to stay on it all the time has been the test. I haven't got back to the pull out with less than a half battery yet.

My notion is that if you have a 14ft boat or less this engine is adequate. No need to break the bank if you're on a budget. For my purposes it is perfect!

The gadget that tilts the thing. Over the years I have fought with those releases. Not so on the MinnKota Endura Transom Mount Trolling Motor. Smoothest one I have ever seen.

The one thing that is not perfect is the reverse. Don't plan on running it from the front of the boat in reverse. Ain't happening. I don't know if the blades aren't pitched right or what, but the reverse really froths the water without giving much ooomph. I mean, it will back you out of the shallows, but it's not for full time use. Forward, on the other hand works just like you like.

About the handle.... Well, I wound up putting my trolling motor in the back and I was kinda worried about steering. You know, twisting around and all. But with the extension handle which you can pull out a lot or a little....it ended up being zero problem. I think I might actually like it more better on the aft now.

And one heads up. If you plan on putting a transducer onto the foot...be advised, it probably won't fit as the foot is too short. However...my workaround was to put my transducer all the way to the rear against the fin and shim it with some rubber pads on an edge so that I got it near to vertical. And my depth finder works just fine. So no harm done. You could use most anything that won't rot. Your wife's Tupperware, for instance.

I like my MinnKota Endura Transom Mount Trolling Motor a LOT and you will too. If your boat be smaller grab one. You'll be thankin' me!
text_fidelity_b: Minn Kota Endura C2 30 Freshwater Transom Mounted Trolling Motor (30" Shaft)

text_fidelity_a:
VP Components VP-Vice Pedals (Pack of 2) There are some interesting patterns that you'll see if you read through the reviews. Some people recevied their pedals shrink wrapped, and they scratch the other pedal in transport. Some people get new pedals in a box, and life is wonderful because they got an awesome pedal set at an awesome price. And some people get pedals in a box that look brand new, but have blown bearings. I'm in that third group.

I bought this pair from cyclingdeal_usa, fulfilled by Amazon. I was happy to see the pedals arrive looking brand new in a box similar to the one my first Vices showed up in about five years ago. I'm a huge fan of these pedals, and the fact that I have a the titanium pins for my primary bike, and that they're now as ridiculously affordable as they are means it makes sense to put these on the other bikes in the house.

I bought these for my son's bike, and the look great, but there was a click with each stroke on the left pedal. I threw them on my bike, on the titanium pins, and there was still a click with each stroke. I changed out the bearings (I had a rebuild kit on hand) and boom, the pedals are exactly as they should be, and the click is gone.

Like some other people's reviews, my VP-Vice Pedal set showed up with blown bearings. The right pedal was fine, but the left pedal clicked out of the box, and that's the first time I've seen a pair of Vice pedals do that. I see they're currently at the best price through VP Components. I'm hopeful that means they're shipped in a new box, and that if there's any issues, I know from a past experience with them, that VP Components will make it right.

I'm rating this purchase 4*, because I love the pedals, I love VP components, and I'm very happy with the bang for the buck of getting all my bikes on Vice pedals, but I hate that I had to use my rebuild kit to get working bearings in left pedal. (Yeah, I know I could have returned them, but I wanted to get them on my son's new bike, and we were all excited to go riding.)
text_fidelity_b: VP Components VP-Vice Pedals (Pack of 2)

text_fidelity_a: Lodge Cast Iron Melting Pot, Pre-Seasoned, 15-Ounce I actually purchased this for mixing henna for my hair rather than for barbecuing. The henna product I use instructed setting the henna in an iron pot, but I thought I could bypass this. After using henna for a couple of months, the thought occurred to me that maybe something in the interaction with the iron metal helps with the curing. Any henna user will tell you that it's an endurance test and everyone has to find their own mixer combination and timing for the results they want. I'm still experimenting, so I bought this pot per the henna instruction with the hope that it will help me get the results I wanted. I did everything in mixing the henna I had usually been doing, then applied it from my roots down about 1". Since I only have to do my roots now, the size of this pot works out. This first time that I have used the pot, the henna color result on my hair is actually a little darker, more red than before without the pot and closer to what I want. I also had kept the henna on my hair for half the time I did before because it was just too hot that day. So, there might be something, then, to the whole iron pot use. Whatever the cause for the darkening, I am continuing with this iron pot and experimenting with combinations. This size is agreeable also because it fits nicely on my small bathroom vanity as I apply the henna and it does not take up much space on my tiny kitchen counter as it cures. The long handle makes it easier to move around, because, well, small bathroom vanity and tiny kitchen counter. I would recommend this pot for anyone who does henna on their roots.

M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch 3-12wt Medium-Fast Action Premier Fly Fishing Rod-IM8 Carbon Blank for High Performance,with AA Cork Grip Hard Chromed Guides and Cordura Tube You see all of these reviews and they all start to sound the same, so I'll tell you where I'm coming from, my thoughts on the rod, and give my verdict.
I love fishing. There's nothing I'd rather do on the whole world. Nothing. You know what I mean... Lol! I've been fishing for decades, but have only been fly fishing for 3 years or so. I have several spinning rods in the $100-$200 range, and they are amazing. Unfortunately a $200 fly rod isn't the same as a $200 spinning rod. You can easily spend $3000 on a high end fly rod!

Well, I don't want to. I don't think it's necessary. But I've been fishing long enough that I can feel a great rod when I handle one. That's good, because I've seen lots of very expensive rods that were trash, and a few hidden gems that punched WAY above their weight. The Maxcatch Premiere line is one of those hidden gems. I picked this 3WT up just to check out, and after I effortlessly my fly 55' and landed it precisely where I wanted it. Over and over again. I mean it is so accurate that it's almost boring lol! And it's a $55 rod!

The blank is very sensitive, very light, very well finished and attractive, and the cork and dark chromed accents are beautiful. I'm surprised at how nice the cork is at this price point!

So I fish. A lot. I used to sell fishing equipment for a living, and I've handle a lot of gear. Is this Maxcatch a Loop or high end Sage? No. But it's also not $400-$900. However, I'd put this up against ANY Reddington, Fenwick, or lower end Sage any day and put money on the Maxcatch.

Get this rod. You'll be glad you did. You'll catch a ton of fish if you do your part, because this is a magnificent tool at an amazing price!

EDIT: I caught that monster 'Bow on the 4wt. Great fight! The rod was bent in half for 5 minutes, and held up great. And I felt every run, head shake, and dive. Great rods!
text_fidelity_b: M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch 3-12wt Medium-Fast Action Premier Fly Fishing Rod-IM8 Carbon Blank for High Performance,with AA Cork Grip Hard Chromed Guides and Cordura Tube

I see a lot of negative reviews of things, but I always temper them with the idea that "most people won't write rave reviews for a product just because it works the way it's supposed to". Meaning people are more likely to write bad reviews than good. So I bought a 330 yd spool of the 6lb "Ultimate Mono". Yipes. So I'm on the water in the canoe, and I start fishing. Trolling close to the bottom, the line snaps. There goes a spinner. But I figured I smashed something. I hate losing terminal tackle, but we all know it happens. Anyway, I begin casting, and as I throw the new spinner out, the line just snaps! Poof! No reason. It's a 3/16oz spinner. Why did it snap?! Still I try to give this Spiderwire the benefit of the doubt. So I try to cast some bottom bait out with a sinker. 1/4oz, a number 4 hook, and some bait. And again, the line snaps mid-cast? I can't believe it! This stuff is awful! Granted, it's very supple and manageable, but none of that matters if you can't get your lure where you want it and have it still attached to your Reel. Do yourself a favor. Save 50%, buy some Trilene XL, and catch some fish!

text_fidelity_a: Intech Golf Swing Impact Bag This impact bag measures 16 inches in diameter and 10 inches tall. It appears to be made of a very durable coated fabric that seems that it would stand up to a lot of use. It has a nylon strap-type handle on the top, under which lies the zipper that is used to install the towels or other soft materials that can be used to fill the bag for use. There is a plastic anchor loop on the bottom that could be used to anchor it to something solid to keep from having to consistently have to chase it after striking it. Now, I must admit that I am an intermediate golfer at best. With that, my main takeaways from using the bag is that it provides a durable, soft impact surface that can be used to swing a club and just practice the swing for purposes such as loosening up after injury, etc. While you could conceivably feel an open or closed club face at impact, I’m not that certain that there is a tremendous amount of actual feedback value that could be gained in reference to the swing. I certainly wouldn’t agree with the promo statement “Use at home to provide same quality practice time as hitting countless balls at the range”. There is also the issue of the noise. If used outside, especially in a fairly populated area, the loud noise that it makes at impact could certainly irritate neighbors. If used inside, I think you’d pretty much have to use earplugs. There may be other users that are more experienced golfers than I that might know of more valuable uses, but as for me, I’ll give it two stars.
text_fidelity_b: Intech Golf Swing Impact Bag

Lifetime 48 Quart High Performance Hard Cooler First, the good: Man, does this thing keep cold. I wanted to test it before I decided to keep it so pre-chilled it with 8 pounds of cold packs, about 5 pounds of 32F (AKA water) freeze point and about 3 pounds of 28F freeze point gel packs. I let this pre-chill the cooler for about 4 hours which lowered the temp down to 40F. I then placed my test ice - 1 quart of water at about 0F - into the cooler. The test ice remained frozen for 2 1/2 days. At the end of the test all of the 32F cooling blocks had thawed but the 28F blocks still had some ice left in them. So, yeah, with some more high-tech ice and filled with more than a quart block of ice this cooler will keep things cold for a long time.

Now, the bad: Come on Lifetime, you make like Made in the USA is a big deal and then you allow seams like the attached photos past quality control. Finish matters. This was a surprise (particularly the open seam) as the rest of cooler seemed really well constructed. I'm not sure if that open seam would allow water into the insulation area but I'm going to slap some sealant on it to be sure it won't. I'll get rid of those rough spots, too.

Otherwise it's a really good cooler, it would have been a solid 5-stars if only it was as well made as the Chinese products.

The knife, as I received it was pretty stiff out ouf the box and did not have a good feel; I almost returned it, but I chose to make some adjustments to the knife that make it flick open and close with great ease.

This is a great knife if you want something that is a small carry but still effective; something you can whip out without looking like a Rambo wannabe

Summary

Tips to optimize this knife as an EDC
- most important, I recommend disassembling this knife and adjusting the liner lock in order to make it easier to get that flick action. To do this, disassemble the knife and give a little bend to the liner lock piece that has the detent ball (google liner lock and detent ball if you need to). It's easy enough to bend with your hands. this will ease the tension as the knife opens and closes.
-I HIGHLY recommend to wrap the pocket clip in a heat shrink tube. I don't remember the exact size, but I had a few lying around the garage. you can pick some up for less than a dollar at any hardware store. If you don't wrap your pocket clip in heat shrink tube, you could seriously scratch your car or other delicate objects if your clip happens to make contact with it. Empower Admittedly, it may seem too early for me to review the Empower Kettlebell & DVD I received yesterday. However, based on past workout purchases, and experiences, I believe this one's a keeper. I went for the 10-pound Kettlebell, and feel this is a good choice. It comes with a DVD with three levels of workouts, starting with one for beginners such as myself. It also includes warmup and cool-down routines, which are highly recommended before and after each workout respectively.

I started today, and after just one workout, I can already feel my core, leg, and arm muscles reacting to workout #1. While I have a little trouble with the 10-pound weight for some of the curl exercises, I modify the exercises to accommodate my lack of strength, and believe the 10-pound bell was a good choice because it allows me more room to grow -- which will be marked by my eliminating the need for modifications before moving on to the second workout.

In facing my 61st birthday, I'm active, and want to stay that way. This is why I'm determined to get in the best shape of my life (even in my early years, I've never been big on exercise). I started a month ago by purchasing a pair of Skecher Shape-ups, and taking brisk walks with my dogs each morning. To break the monotony, I purchased an MP3 player, and download books from the library. The time flies by!

I added resistance weeks ago with a trip to the gym, intent on going and working out every other day. Then reality hit. It took too long to get dressed, get my walk in, and then go to the gym, work out, come home and clean up. My mornings were shot. So I needed another way to achieve my goal.

A friend told me about Kettlebells. Now, after just one short Kettlebell workout, I've accomplished as much as when using several machines at the gym. The best part is it's fast. I can hop out of bed, and get it done quickly.

Based on numerous past workout experiences and money wasted on a variety of machines and other programs and gimmicks, I'm convinced this is what I've been searching for. I'd recommend it to anyone thinking of starting to get in shape, and wanting fast results. If you're new to working with weights, which I am not, you might want to start with the Empower 5-Pound KettleBell with DVD, and then work your way up to heavier Kettlebells. text_fidelity_a:
XGrid XGS9USB 9W Portable Solar Panel and USB/LED Flashlight Kit At first I was really excited to get this product, mainly because the idea of using two solar panels to energize a dying cell phone, netbook, or any other device using solar power appealed to me as a novelty. The set feels well-made, each part (the FLEX USB Regular and XGB3L Battery Pack and flashlight) rubberized for protection and assumedly waterproof as well. The panels can be folded up and put into your backpack like a folder, so it doesn't take up too much room.

In terms of functionality, however, I found that using my much-smaller Duracell Powermat does just as good a job of recharging my cell phone when I'm on a trip as this much larger solar panel (and it doesn't require sunlight, just a day in advance to charge it up before a trip). Moreover, the powermat fits in the palm of my hand.

The main advantage this product has over my Powermat is that it has the capacity to power your tablet and larger PC devices as well. The flashlight is a nice touch, but if I bring a flashlight with me with new batteries installed, it's also unlikely I'd have to use solar power for the flashlight either.

So, unless you plan on reading your Kindle or using your Tablet a lot while camping, or expect to be on a long trip in the wilderness or desert where you are unlikely to find a place to recharge a phone after exhausting several powermat-like devices, I would just throw a couple of powermat devices into my bag. Also, weather is never predictable, so if you happen to have the misfortune of traveling on days where it's cloudy or overcast, you might well find yourself stuck with a dead device. As a result, I'd rather pack several small, fully-charged powermats.

I really wanted to like this product, but I found that I like the idea of it (using solar panels) more than the practicality of using this device. However, please note I am speaking as a camper who rarely goes on a trip longer than a week, and doesn't expect to use my phone or tablet all that much while away.
text_fidelity_b: XGrid XGS9USB 9W Portable Solar Panel and USB/LED Flashlight Kit

But to be honest? I burn a lot of Morning Star stick incense which fits perfectly between the electrodes of the TekFire. I got tired of grill/barbeque lighters with more safeties than some guns a few required two hands to operate or cheap lighters that even half full stop working after a few uses. I saw this rechargeable fuel-less lighter and have found i perfect for lighting my incense and tea lights as well as tall candles and oil lamps rather nicely. Durability is something we're going to have to see over time. The lighter comes with a two year warranty so there's plenty of time to give it a workout and see how it performs. So far? I'm very happy with this item.

Edit 10-06-2017 - This is sold as survival/camping gear. I simply use it around the house to light small candles and stick incense which small are a fairly tight fit between the electrodes. If this is meant for outdoor use why would they put a cheap, fragile and easily broken clear plastic hinge on the unit? Mine, after less than a month is severely wobbly. I would have no faith this would survive long term camping trips. I take care of my gear, as an example my backpack (a Jansport Eiger) is well over 30 years old. My sheath knife is similarly aged and even has my name and Explorer Post number scratched into the back of the sheath. I can't imagine this lighter lasting two years let alone 30+. I'm ready for the hinge to break any day now. I've dropped my review by one star due to poor quality/construction.

G4Free 2/4/13 PCS Camping Cookware Mess Kit Hiking Backpacking Picnic Cooking Bowl Non Stick Pot Knife Spoon Set This is a decent set of camping cookware consisting of four pots, each with handles (but no lids). The set nestles together into a pretty compact stack that measures about 7 inches tall and about 5 inches wide. It also comes with a mesh pouch to hold the pots when they are stacked together. It makes for a small, easily toted package.

The build quality is decent but not exceptional. The pans are aluminum and somwhat thin. The metal is thick enough so that the pots won't dent easily, but you can flex the pan if you squeeze them hard. The handles have a silicon coating on them which is nice for helping with heat protection (although you still need a mitt or pad to grab the handle if the pot has been on the fire for a while). The handles fold easily and take up very little room. However, the bracket that attaches the handles to the pot, as well as the handles themselves, are not all that sturdy. They are functional, but won't stand up to much (or any) abuse.

The pot sizes are fine for cooking for one or two people (perhaps you could stretch it to three if everyone is a light eater).

For occasional camping (or the rare emergency) use, these are more than durable enough to get the job done, and do so in a very space-conservative fashion. For that, I'd give them 4-stars. If, however, you're an especially avid camper, or need to cook for more than two people, you'll probably want a larger, more durable set.
[Sample provided for review]

ETROL Mini First Aid Kit - Upgrade 117 Piece Personal Compact Emergency Survival Kits,Lightweight Portable Essential Medical Supplies for Car Backpacking Camping Home Travel Boat The information provided in the written part of the product description needs to line up with the pictures as well as what is actually sent. It is NOT THE SAME as what you read or see. There are some spots that are the same, and many that are different. I CAN NOT RECOMMEND THIS based on the mixed information.

HERE IS WHAT I RECEIVED:
--A smooth, zippered soft "hard shell" case (firm but flexible. Think of a cheap sunglass case). This is not at all what is pictured NOR described in the product information. What is pictured is a totally different material. It may not make a difference if you are just looking for some supplies, OR it may make all the difference if you are looking for a particular container as well as supplies. With this as the description, "Durable & Portable Tactical Molle Pouch】ETROL mini Survival Gear is ultralight, compact and portable with a Velcro strap system compatible with MOLLE so that it can be hooked to the backpack, belt or other. It offers large compartments and plenty of room to add your own equipment, including a special phone pocket and an emergency pen slot" NOPE NOPE NONE OF THIS. Just a smooth zippered shell. No means to use it as part of MOLLE system, no extra compartments or special pockets or place to have a pen. They are describing a product even different than shown, and even further off from what I received.

--The product description also states (as of 3/31/20) that, "【Quick Access & Top Quality Durable Supplies】The Survival Gear Kit includes the most popular outdoor survival necessities: 3-mode Tactical Flashlight, black stainless steel Tactical Military Knife, Fire Starter, Compass of the military class, a Multi-Function Tool Card, a loudly Whistle with 120db, Emergency Blankets which can retain 90% of body heat and more. Being customized and uniquely tested, our Survival First Aid Kit is designed to prepare you well in case of outdoor activities " NOPE!! Plastic whistle and emergency blanket, yes. Flashlight, military knife, fire starter, compass, Multi function tool card.. NOPE. I actually didn't expect this, but for it to state this in the description? False advertisement!

Kit is described as measuring 7.5" x 5.1" x 2"
MY KIT measures roughly, 6.5" x 4.75" x 2.5"

--The product description DOES seem to accurately state the medical supplies portion, "【FDA Approved & Professional Treatment Supplies】This First Aid Kit contains the most important first aid supplies for various treatments on the market. Buckle Tourniquet, PBT conforming bandage, Tourniquet, non-woven tape, first aid scissors, plastic tweezers, sterile gauze, a lot of alcohol swabs, cotton swabs, PE adhesive bandages, and safety pins, to stop massive bleeding, dressing or disinfection of wounds nd more, which will come in handy in case of unforeseen events". To see what you are getting, I can say that it 100% matches up to the product description PICTURE of the supplies. ((NOT THE CASE, though))

Furthermore,
--The kit I have has a fairly useless first aid manual. It is labeled as being by "Firstar" (as are the medical packaging), and is visually messy as well as minimally informative. Consider it non essential and add your own emergency steps. As for the contents, again, it is as described according to the product description and pictures. YET If compared to the information provided on the manual, it would not come close to being the same items. For what it is worth, what comes in this kit according to the product description picture is much better.

--Other plusses include that I am pleased with all that is in there, how well it is packed, how easy it is to access the items as well as how surprisingly easy it was to get everything back into the container.

--However I take issue with the misinformation between what is described and what I received. Even if they totally took out the part on all the tactical goodies that is supposed to be in it, and just focused on the medical.. then there would still be the problem of the TOTALLY DIFFERENT case than what is pictured and described. The soft/hard shell zippered case is OK enough, and would be FINE if it were pictured and described as such. But if you are expecting a MOLLE bag/attach capable (that's a big thing), then this would be hugely disappointing.

--So overall, I can not in good conscience recommend a product when it is so far off from what is pictured and described. I have no idea what it costs, and you better believe that a MOLLE style/attachment capable bag is worth more than this soft/hard shell.

--I would include pictures but the photo/video uploader that Amazon usually has in the reviews has been missing for about a week now. If I see that it comes back up, I will be sure to show you the case I have, then you can see how different it is. Again, case is a firm smooth soft shell with zipper. Bright red and labeled, "first aid kit"

If the product description (plus pic of the container) changes, then I can edit this as is reasonable.

Again-- the actual contents according to the picture/graphic is correct. The case is not. The description of the case and other items is entirely wrong. The list of items this kit contains according to the useless weird manual is also wrong, BUT the items included here are better. SO do with this information as you will. I hope it helped you today. Despite the errors in information, it is possible that what I described happens to be exactly what you are looking for. My 1 star rating could be your 5 :)
text_fidelity_b: ETROL Mini First Aid Kit - Upgrade 117 Piece Personal Compact Emergency Survival Kits,Lightweight Portable Essential Medical Supplies for Car Backpacking Camping Home Travel Boat

Backyard Champs Corn Hole Outdoor Game: 2 Folding Cornhole Boards and 8 Bean Bags, Aluminum Frame with MDF Board Cornhole is a fun game that brings back memories of “Toss-Across” for me. I never had heard of, or played, cornhole until it was introduced to me at a social gathering relatively recently. I have wanted my own set for taking to family functions and picnics with friends, and this set is well suited for these situations.

I will start with this: I received the tailgate version which is a little smaller than the regulation size set. The difference is that the boards are a foot shorter. That’s ok, but it does mean that my set is not suitable for true tournament play and instead is geared for casual competition. Both sized sets are available here; make sure you get the size you want. While it may be a little smaller, it has two distinct advantages. First, it is lighter so it is easier to carry. Second, because it is smaller it is more compact and can be stored (and transported) more easily too.

This set is made to be portable. Most sets I have seen have been made of plywood and have fixed legs. To move them is awkward and often unwieldy. This set instead has an aluminum frame and lightweight boards so the weight is substantially reduced. The legs fold under, allowing the set to lay flat. This makes it a lot easier to pack the set for travel and to store it away when not in use. An important detail – when the legs are down they lock in place with a metal bracket so the board will not collapse.

The set comes with 8 bean bags, 4 blue and 4 red. These are regulation size and are interchangeable with other sets.

So far my family is very pleased with this set. It is made very well, it is compact and portable, and because this set (in my case) is the tailgate version it is lighter and easier to store when not in use. This is an easy product to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Backyard Champs Corn Hole Outdoor Game: 2 Folding Cornhole Boards and 8 Bean Bags, Aluminum Frame with MDF Board

text_fidelity_a: attwood 10556-5 Marine Canvas Cover Repair Kit, Grey Pretty easy to use.  I had two holes in my boat cover that needed repairing.  The material that comes w/this kit seems heavy duty.  Just cut a piece to fit.  I tried applying the included glue two different ways, either was recommended by the directions.  For the first hole I applied a thin layer of glue to the entire patch and stuck it over the hole in my cover.  For the second hole I applied the glue to the cover and applied the patch over the hole and glue.  The later method seemed a lot messier w/a lot of glue outside of the patch, as it's hard to apply it exactly in the same place the patch will stick.  In the end, the patch stuck to the boat cover just the same.  So, I would recommend spreading a thin layer on the entire patch and then stick the patch over the hole in the cover.  The glue dries pretty quick, but no so quick you cannot work w/it.  As of now, my patches seem to have adhered to the cover pretty well. text_fidelity_a:

I first purchased the 45" version but realized those did not work on my trailer so I replaced with the 65" which is perfect. I have a 19.5' I/O runabout boat with tandem wheel aluminum trailer. I mainly bought so I could see the trailer without the boat when backing, but also use this for loading in wind and/or in deeper water where you can't see the back of the trailer.

This product is strong, reinforced at the corners, metal tubing running up nearly all the way into the PVC, heavy duty PVC and mounting brackets. Those fit a variety of sizes of trailers.

It is not galvanized however, but zinc plated. It will not last in salt water so opt for something different if planning to be in salt or brackish water.

I gave mine a quick waxing before installation (all metal parts) just to add another layer of protection.

Installation was simple. I installed mine under the trailer frame instead of on top. I did have to buy the optional longer bolts based on the instructions, however, the bolts that came with the basic package would have fit. But overall everything was easy, simple and quick to install.

Very professional looking and I would highly recommend, especially over those that only use a small amount of metal going up into the PVC. These can take a good amount of force from your boat.

text_fidelity_a:
Pelican 14 Quart Cooler This is a top brand. Know for travel and camera cases and even mobile phone cases.

Love the color. Recently used for the beach. Has a top compartment where keys, phones, and a kindle can fit.

Inside came with a tray which others can charge up to 20+ for.

Of course at 14qt not a ton of storage but a few beers, and wine coolers, sandwiches and snacks worked out well at beach.
Pelican even has their own ice packs that fit this model similar to Yeti.

Handle has good grip and easy to carry. Loaded up, little heavy. There is no "lock in place " on handle so it moves as your moving with in hand if you sway.

Built in can opener which came in handy at beach for beer bottles. It was sort of hidden but in middle.

Nicest feature, the push button latches! Work great no struggle with the rubber latches on others. This feature, along with top (almost hidden) compartment were reason I bought this.

Cons
This is by design (14qt) the ice melt rating is almost 2 days not 5 like other brands. For us, didn't matter as it's for car trips, beach fun and it does great job. Used Pelican ice packs and open and close several times at beach, the beer was ice cold. After several hours ice packs still frozen and contents cold.

I would buy again when on sale and also go to next model up as it's taller to fit wine bottles. Didn't see the need for 200+ for that as have larger 45 model from another brand that works great for larger needs.
text_fidelity_b: Pelican 14 Quart Cooler

text_fidelity_a:
New Balance Unisex, Men's and Women's Running Stash Hat with Zippered Pocket, for Athletic and Fashion Wear, One Size Fits Most Pros:
FIT: It's very lightweight, cushion is good, and does not feel awkward or too tight/loose due to the manual adjustment strap. I've forgotten I've had it on several times until I pour water on my head during 90+ deg F summer runs.

MATERIALS: The mesh top combined with moisture-wicking material of the hat's construction makes this a must-have gear for my Texas summer running season, where pouring water on one's head is necessary.

WICKING: It does soak up some head sweat, but won't 100% eliminate the need for a headband or vaseline for humid days if you sweat a lot. The hat also dries out very quickly. I hang it on a wall in my garage, fully-saturated in sweat + drinking water and it's always dry in 12-24 hours for my next run.

POCKET: it's small and I haven't used it yet but perfect size for a key fob or even a small gel.

CONS:
WHITE/VIBRANT ORANGE: if you sweat profusely like me, the orange piping will bleed a little on this hat. Not obnoxious enough to be an issue for me, but for those that are OCD about that kinda thing, it's worth noting.

STYLE: I have a large head (7 3/8), so unstructured hats look much better on me than taller sitting hats. That said, this hat is extremely unstructured, by nature, and is not going to win any fashion awards for most head shapes. It's got a distinct "this has a very specific function" style.
text_fidelity_b: New Balance Unisex, Men's and Women's Running Stash Hat with Zippered Pocket, for Athletic and Fashion Wear, One Size Fits Most

text_fidelity_a:
[New Arrival] Cocoweb TraiLead 3 Bike Hitch-Mount Bike Rack The rack is solid. Really easy to attach to the hitch. In our case I have to problem whatsoever to attach it when we need it and remove it right after use using the included hardware. One review mentioned that leaves it exposed to a theft, so I tossed a wrench and remove the rack while we are biking (it takes about a minute). Perhaps the greatest feature are those bike cradles and straps. We transport 3 bikes - 1 men frame, 1 women and 1 children's. They all hang at different angles, but all 3 are very solid and unmovable. The collapsible frame is a nice feature too. Once I forgot to close the door while I already had one bike attached to the rack (yeah, I was tired after a long ride :-)) Lowered the rack with that bike on it, closed the door, return the rack back to upright position and kept loading the remaining 2 bikes.

The only (perceived maybe) con of this rack - it is a bit wobbly when it is loaded and the car is moving. When I keep that in mind and drive a bit more carefully that does not appear to be an issue. Note that bikes are attached securely and do not move at all even a little bit relative to each other or to the frame. But the entire thing wobbles slightly left and right when the car moves on an uneven pavement. I do not think this is a hitch connector issue as it fits snugly into a hitch receiver. Could be that the 1.25" to 2" adapter just cannot provide enough support. Or maybe that's the inherent weakness of hitch-mounted racks (the connection to the receiver cannot be rigid enough). Or both... Take into account that this is our first rack and I have no experience whatsoever with other racks. They probably all wobble, I just do not have a good reference to say whether this wobbles more or less.
text_fidelity_b: [New Arrival] Cocoweb TraiLead 3 Bike Hitch-Mount Bike Rack

text_fidelity_a:
Agility Training Equipment, Speed Training Equipment Kit with Adjustable Hurdles,12 Rungs,1 Reaction Ball,20 Disc Cones and Resistance Parachute,for Football, Basketball, Hockey All Training Athletes My son just started soccer and the other started teeball and you are probably thinking what does this have to do with speed and agility? Everything.

I needed something fun but also challenging for them because it became more of a training game than training.

Hurdles:
These are tricky but friendly in that they hold up well, especially for when you are moving over them quickly. I enjoy these for building rebounding strength for explosiveness. The kids were not big fans because they can be tedious to not tag one with your foot.

Cones:
We did zig zags as well as 4 corners and a T drill. These drills help more with being reactive and help with bursts after a transition. You can improve on these in terms of improving time but the focus really should be on building the ability to move quickly (especially moving laterally - sideways).

Ladder:
Think of being light on your feet and getting used to pushing off the ball of your foot. Fast feet is the key. This is like the cone drill where being good at this specific obstacle doesn't help much but as part of being "quick" repetition does help (that may sound counterintuitive). If it helps with anything other than fast feet, it's the ability to not trip over your own feet as you are moving around the field of play.

Jump Rope:
Helps build coordination and feeling like you are training like Rocky Balboa.

Resistance Bands:
These are great for building hip strength but ideal to use during the warmup phase versus active training.

Obstacle Ball:
This helps really build hand-eye coordination and a solid floor is key (along with keeping your parents lamps out of the way).

Parachute:
Parachute training tends to look cooler than it is BUT this was THE MOST FUN part of getting my kids to enjoy training. We did this part of the "obstacle" course last. They loved watching the chute burst open and each other running in slow motion.

Sorry for the instruction but it was also how I helped my kids understand getting their feet moving and the goal. Other than that the quality is fantastic and flexible (things won't break easily) The parachute can be a little tedious to unwind/wind back up, but it is what they look forward to in training.

SO incredibly pleased with this purchase!
text_fidelity_b: Agility Training Equipment, Speed Training Equipment Kit with Adjustable Hurdles,12 Rungs,1 Reaction Ball,20 Disc Cones and Resistance Parachute,for Football, Basketball, Hockey All Training Athletes

text_fidelity_a:
YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments My wife and I prefer weights as a workout, but both of us find the handles our community provides for the lat pull to be uncomfortable. The community provides the bar and nylon strap options, but 1. even with leather gloves they are uncomfortable, and 2. as a shorter guy my arm span is not such that I can get and maintain a comfortable reach (I can't hold the rubber grips on the bar), so for safety and comfort, I'm outta luck. But when I saw this YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for the gym I thought it might help me with comfort and safety, and be something she and I could both use to help improve.

The YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment is as easy as any attachment for the lat pull to get on and off, fitting the community's machine easily. There is a concern we have, but only time will tell if it plays out: the connection has a plastic exterior over what appears to be a metal disk, but we cannot tell how far that metal extends. It SEEMS as though it is only a disk and that the majority of the top piece is plastic. So we are not sure for how long or how much weight this connector will last. It is not that we have "proof" of it being subpar, just concerning by appearance.

The material of the rope itself also seems, not as overall strong, but as we are not at all experts in these materials or what is common in most of the heavy work gyms, we have nothing to compare it to. So we are going with it being an appropriate set up and provided materials. For our level of weights, even as I get stronger, we don't see it being at all an issue.

Lastly is the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment's handgrip, where you get that ergonomic element. I attempt to show in the various images how it is structured, curveted for the hand to rest within, allowing for a strong and comfortable grip. Again, I'm a shorter guy, so I also have a smaller hand. My wife's fingers are slightly longer than mine. We each find that the grip is both good and bad. We can each grip it and feel we have a secure hold. We feel safe. We feel a great pull. However, we each have a spot on the grip where it cuts into our finger/hand and begins to rub. In two images I show 1. the grip itself as I hold it up, then 2. my thumb over the top - it is at this point for me where it rubs and begins to feel like it's cutting into the thumb. Again, it is my hand size. My wife's issue is in the palm. She can fully and comfortably grip the handle, but at the base of the palm there is a cutting pressure.

So, do we like the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment? Yes, very much.
In spite of the issue and admittedly, with only using it twice for our full reps, we do like it. I will add, we have not worn our gloves during these workouts. We normally do, but circumstances had us in there without them, so using our bare hands, we did come up with discomfort whereby we got through the workouts, but didn't go full out as the discomfort grew. BUT, we both feel like once we have on the leather gloves the issue will at the least decrease greatly enough so as to allow us a full on workout and be okay. I will update if that does not pan out. But for each of us, the better grip and the overall feel of the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment as far as what we can do, how safe we feel, and even comfort to the greater part of our hands is enough. We went with the 4 star because of the issue, but WE THINK THAT if they were to add a more comfortable cushion (rubber, something) to the grip, this would be a great 5 star grip.
text_fidelity_b: YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments

text_fidelity_a:
Victagen USB Rechargeable Bike Light Sets, Rechargeable Super Bright 2400 Lumens Front Light with Rechargeable Bike Tail Light, Helmet Light, Waterproof Bike Headlamp, Easy Mount Remove and Rotatable Like most low-priced LED lights on amazon, this one overstates its lumen output by quite a bit. Usually they are using LED which are rated up to 2400 lumens but they are not driving them with enough wattage to produce that much light. I have several expensive lights from other manufacturers like Light & Motion and ITUO which I know to be rated accurately. Comparing this light to my ITUO Wiz XP3 (2300 lumens) it is clear that this light is nowhere near as bright. However, comparing to my L&M 1200 lumen light, this one is pretty similar in brightness. The Light & Motion light has a wider beam pattern which is better for cycling.. but this Victagen model performs pretty well and for the price it is an excellent value.

Pros:
Full aluminum enclosure, good for heat dissipation
Weather sealed with Silicon grommets
Rear Battery indicator LEDs
the 2 internal 18650 batteries can be replaced** (see note below)
very bright for the price (true output around 1000-1200 lumens which is plenty bright for most uses)
includes 2 mounts

Cons:
narrow beam pattern, this is somewhat offset by having two LEDs, but it would still be greatly improved by diffusing optics or different reflectors

** Note regarding the 18650 batteries -- you can disassemble this light and replace the internal batteries (they are standard 18650 flat top style); however, it is somewhat easy to break the internal wiring when reassembling if you are not careful, so I would not recommend hot swapping the batteries while on a ride. Even though it is not great for hot-swapping, it is nice to have the option to replace the batteries later if the included ones start to fade quickly, or to replace with higher capacity cells for even more run-time.
text_fidelity_b: Victagen USB Rechargeable Bike Light Sets, Rechargeable Super Bright 2400 Lumens Front Light with Rechargeable Bike Tail Light, Helmet Light, Waterproof Bike Headlamp, Easy Mount Remove and Rotatable

SOG Tactical Tomahawk- Throwing Hatchet, Versatile Survival Tactical Axe and Emergency Breaching Tool with Sheath (F01TN-CP) In Vietnam, American Special Forces soldiers soon learned a lesson their ancestors knew very well--a tomahawk is better than a knife for close combat. In spite of its popularity, my own opinion of the Vietnam tomahawk has always been that it's a wimpy little ax, with a head that's too small for real work and a handle that will snap like a twig. It's a crude blunt instrument that looks like an ax. The SOG Fusion Tactical Tomahawk takes the concept behind the Vietnam Special Forces ax and gets rid of the many problems.

Weight is a major concern whether you are a hunter or a soldier, and you need a lot of positives to carry a 24 oz axe as a regular part of your kit. The SOG Fusion justifies every ounce. The steel ax head, with the traditional military spike for balance, has a 2 3/4" straight edge that's properly ground so you can efficiently chop wood or heavy bone. Hunters of big game often find a small ax to be more efficient at butchering tasks than a heavy knife, something nearly everyone knew in the frontier days.

The weakest point of the old Vietnam axe was the wooden handle, too thin at the juncture with the axe head to be reliable. The Fusion has a much less destructible fiberglass handle with rubberized grip. Once marketed as "unbreakable," fiberglass proved to be much less than perfect as a tool handle. The tang and rivet attachment of head to handle that you see in the Fusion is an excellent solution to the old issue of head separation, a puzzle that smiths have battled for centuries. Used with some skill, this combination really should last forever. In camp you'll find it's endlessly practical.
text_fidelity_b: SOG Tactical Tomahawk- Throwing Hatchet, Versatile Survival Tactical Axe and Emergency Breaching Tool with Sheath (F01TN-CP)

Skechers Women's GO Walk High Waisted Legging As a Lululemon aficionado, I'm frequently disappointed by the pants offerings from other companies. But where Lululemon falls short is that they rarely put pockets on their high waisted pants, leaving me trying to find weird solutions to keep my cell phone on me, such as a cell phone pocket scarf, a cell phone lanyard that is worn around the neck, armbands, etc. I don't want all of that business, I just want to put my phone in my pocket. I have to keep it on me constantly for work, so it's important to me.

So I was absolutely delighted to see that skechers has come out with this offering of awesome, high waisted pants that actually stay put and do not slip down, that have two generously sized pockets! The material is medium thick and completely not see-through, like the old-school Lululemon fabric used to be, hides any number of lumps and bumps, is just compressive enough to feel flattering and comfortable yet not so compressive that I feel sweaty and eager to take the pants off. The high waist has a normal larger waistband like most types of yoga pants with this cut, but then they also have an additional elastic band that runs right around the top, which really holds the pants in place. It does cause a little bit of a belly roll where it sits, but usually my shirt hides it and it's worth it to not have to pull my pants up constantly throughout the day, especially when they are holding up my heavy cell phone as well.

I am usually a size 8 in Lululemon pants, which puts me right between a size medium and a size large in this brand. I feel like the medium is just a little too tight, and the large has a little extra fabric around the crotch. I settled on the medium for actually working out, and the large for lounging around the house, since I would usually lounge with a long tunic top any way and would prefer to be comfortable. I wish that they came in numbered sizing rather than small medium large sizing, so that there would be more size options in between medium and large.

However, if a person is lucky enough to fit squarely into one of the sizes, I think these pants would make most women happy. When they first arrived, they looked slightly short and cropped, but they actually fit me like full-sized pants, I think they stretch lengthwise once you put them on.
text_fidelity_b: Skechers Women's GO Walk High Waisted Legging

text_fidelity_a:
Altus Athletic 3lb. Fitness Hoops Based on the other reviews, I expected to be extremely disappointed in this Altus Fitness Hoop. However, I absolutely adore this product because assembly is easy (see ASSEMBLY CAUTION note below) and since the hoop is weighted it is easy to keep going while doing the regular "hula hoop" motion. The hoop also has an all foam exterior so it cushions the impact on your mid-section.

I was able to do the traditional core excercise for 20 minutes straight without a problem. The only issue I had was that my mid-section felt sore because of the constant weight that was rotating around my stomach and waist. (The instructions warn of this for first time users.)

The hoop is a bit large and you have to use all the alternating color segments when assembling, so you can't make it smaller. It is about about 2-3 inches larger in circumference than my regular adult hula hoop which fit snugly inside the circumference of this hoop. As a result, I had to use this in the parking lot of my condo complex because I had no room in the house. This resulted in some spectators, of course.

Besides doing my core exercise in public, I also tried to do the arm exercises with the hoop. However, due to the weight I was unable to; but then again I never used a hula hoop any other way other than on my hips and that is all I wanted this for.

Other than the soreness I felt due to the rotating weight, this hoop is lots of fun. I can't vouch for the claim that it will imporve core strength and trim your waist, but I suppose that it might if you do it longer enough over a couple of months. When I hula my movement is very subtle so I doubt I'm burning more than a few calories. However, if you really gyrate when you hula, then you'll get more of a workout with this device.

ASSEMBLY CAUTION: The assembly instructions that came with this product are extremely poor. The way to assemble this hoop so that it does not come apart is to insert each segment into the previous segment and make sure that the "segment's release button" for each segment on your RIGHT is slightly protruding under the foam where the button connector dots are located for each segment on the LEFT. To test, twist (in an up and down motion) the left and right segments you just connected and also try to pull the segments in the opposite direction. If neither segment twists or pulls apart, then they are securely connected. Repeat this procedure for each segment of the hoop. Not once did this hoop fall apart on me. However, had I not done the twist and pull test, it would have fallen apart repeatedly because it takes some finagling to get each segment in place securely. Although this hoop is easy to assemble it still took me about 10-15 minutes to assemble the entire hoop since I made about 4 attempts and 4 tests per left and right segment to get the segments securely connected so they wouldn't fall off no matter how hard I pulled or twisted.

May 14 Update: I've been using this hoop every day except one for over a week now and still love it. It has not come apart once. Due to the weight of the hoop hitting against my body on rotation, I did develop a one inch bruise on my right hip. Other than this brusie I don't have any negative effects and the soreness I experienced when I used it the first time has gone away completely. I absolutely love this fitness hula hoop. Although I don't think I'm losing any weight from this, I find it a lot of fun and it's worth it just for that. One caveat - if you have cats (or dogs), don't leave the hoop where they can reach it. I put mine by the door a few minutes before I went out with it and my cats chewed through the soft foam on one segment of the hoop. The foam is easily destructible.
text_fidelity_b: Altus Athletic 3lb. Fitness Hoops

PRETTYGAGA Plus Holds Cell Phone，Outdoor Tactical， Messenger Bag， Military Trekking As a woman who wants to enjoy the concealed carry option but doesn’t want to carry an extra purse for cell phone, cash, etc., I have to say this little case takes care of it all. It has so much functionality that I almost don’t know where to start.

Laying flat and without anything in it, this very durable and well-made nylon case measures about 7-1/2” wide x 9-1/2” tall. That also includes a gusset which, when extended, accommodates a pretty good sized gun. Almost all the seams are double-stitched, and an outer strong and durable bungee style closure keeps the pockets on the outer side of the purse secure. In addition to the larger inner pocket where you can stash your weapon (or if not a weapon will hold quite a bit of other things), there is also a front outer pocket that is perfect for a cell phone. My Galaxy J7 fits great. Another great feature is you have the option of carrying this case like a purse with the removable strap, or you can remove the strap and wear on your belt.

There is a wide band of Velcro in the front of the case which, when opened reveals 10 card slots (including 1 clear for I.D.), a zippered pocket which is perfect size for cash bills, and a pocket behind each set of card slots where you can store coupons, receipts, etc. **I do want to note that while the zipper pouch is great for bills, it may not be great for loose change because if you unzipper the bill slot with the case in upright/vertical position which it would be if you are wearing it, and loose change may fall out. There is also a zipper pocket right at the very top of the purse actually at the top of the front flap. Unzip that and you’ll find a great little pocket for an extra magazine (or 2-3 depending on the size). It could also be a good pocket to hold your keys. On the back side of this pouch there is another zipper compartment that can easily hold a larger size cell phone or extra ammo mags or even your gun depending on the size.

Overall, this is a great case that can be used by men or women, and I can’t find anything that I don’t like about it. It’s a keeper!

text_fidelity_a:
Sigma Sport BC8.12 8 Function Bicycle Computer This computer never truly turns off so the battery will go dead and need to be replaced sooner than it should. After a few minutes of inactivity the screen display changes to show the time, and the computer constantly monitors for movement of the wheel. When it detects movement, it turns the speed/distance display on automatically. I know that these devices do not use much electricity, but there really is no reason that I cannot turn the display on and off manually, or at least have it automatically turn to a hard shut down after inactivity and turn on manually. Are bicyclists so lazy they cannot press a button to start their computer? Manufacturers of electronic devices have become lazy and foist devices with phantom loads on their customers. Perhaps I am more sensitive to wasted electricity than most people because I live off grid.

The installation is easy. I am a bit concerned how well the rubber band-like o-rings that hold the main components to the bicycle will hold up in sunlight. They seem like a bit of excessive cost-cutting in the manufacturing process.

If you have disk brakes you will need to mount the sensor on the fork on the side opposite the brake disk in order to have the proper clearance -- spokes on the disk side are likely to be too far from the fork.

The display is easily readable at a glance, even for the eyes of this old rider who relies on reading glasses, and even riding my mountain bike over extremely rough, rocky roads. The display is simple so one can quickly and easily spot the important information one wants. The single button makes it easy to scroll through the displays.

There are other computers available for not much more money that have many additional functions, but few people really need anything more than this, and adding functions just makes it more difficult to find on the go the data one is seeking.

It is easy to spend 2 or 3 times as much and still have no more than what this unit does. So while it is not perfect, it offers excellent value, I would buy it again over any of its competition, and I recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Sigma Sport BC8.12 8 Function Bicycle Computer
